findings.title: Public entry serves the API without TLS
findings.description: The public entry (Ingress, load balancer, Istio Gateway or published port) has no TLS, so Authorization headers and personal data sent through it can be read or replayed on the network. The evidence says how many public endpoints carried them in this capture.
findings.detail: LoadBalancer Service frontend-external serves the API over plain HTTP
findings.recommendation: Enable TLS on LoadBalancer Service frontend-external.
mitigation: Terminate TLS at the ingress (tls: section + certificate) and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
Send Strict-Transport-Security so browsers never fall back to HTTP.
findings.snippet:
spec:
  tls:
    - hosts: [api.example.com]
      secretName: api-tls

findings.title: Service-to-service call accepted without credentials
findings.description: Another microservice calls this endpoint without any credential and it succeeds, so any pod that can reach it can do the same (no zero-trust between services).
findings.detail: frontend -> POST /hipstershop.AdService/GetAds (adservice) with no credential
factors: likelihood -1: reachable only inside the cluster
evidence: no mTLS enforced for adservice (no STRICT PeerAuthentication or mesh injection)
findings.recommendation: Require service identity (mTLS or a service token) on /hipstershop.AdService/GetAds in adservice.
mitigation: Authenticate workloads to each other: mTLS through a service mesh, or signed service tokens.
Authorize per caller: only order-service may call /charge, for example.
findings.snippet:
# Istio: require mTLS and allow only order-service
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
spec:
  rules:
  - from:
    - source: {principals: ["cluster.local/ns/shoplite/sa/order-service"]}
